hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge into the output with a 3x3 conv adds a whole learnable path, a much larger gain than replacing another op.
Adding a conv on the direct input-to-output edge where none existed gives a large gain compared with swapping an existing op.
Turning a missing edge into a 3x3 conv adds capacity and a path, unlike replacing an existing op.
Edge 2 starts at node 1, which receives input only through edge 0, so a conv there does little when edge 0 is none.
Edge 4 carries nothing useful from node 1 when edge 0 is none, so the conv edit helps less.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 cannot reach the output, so a conv on edge 2 is wasted.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv on the direct edge to skip loses capacity, a worse change than replacing a weaker op.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the final edge with skip hurts more than replacing a weaker op.
Edge 0 is the only entry to node 1, so replacing none with a conv activates the whole branch via node 1.
Replacing none with a conv on edge 1 opens a new input path to node 2, a larger gain than swapping ops.
